clue.text: Liberal Democrat genius showing dejection

indicators.note: liberal means free and unconstrained, so the letters that follow are taken loosely and rearranged

blocks.note: the fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A brilliant Lib Dem politician looks thoroughly downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal Democrat' reads as one party name, but 'Liberal' is split off to signal the anagram of DEMOCRAT GENIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Discouragement is a state of low spirits, a close synonym for dejection.

clue.text: Doctor wearing uniform interrupted by two Americans, each providing basin

indicators.note: something interrupted has other material breaking into it, so the two letters are set inside the phrase before

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for doctor
someone wearing clothes is in them
gear is clothing, such as a uniform
A is an abbreviation for American, taken twice
EA is the commercial abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: A uniformed doctor is held up by two Americans who each bring a washing bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The two single-letter Americans break into the doctor-wearing-uniform phrase at two separate points, one on each side of the word for wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A river basin is the whole region of land that drains into that river, its drainage area.

clue.text: Women's group's punching Nazis from European nation

indicators.note: a fist punching goes into its target, so one piece is pushed inside the other

blocks.note: the WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation, plus the 's
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: A women's group attacks Nazis who came from somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British community organisation for women, abbreviated WI.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss is the adjective for something coming from Switzerland, a European country.

clue.text: Put too much effort in fixing vote to welcome king and queen

indicators.note: fixing a vote means rigging it, so its letters are tampered with and rearranged
to welcome is to take guests in, so the shuffled letters surround the royal pair

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
Rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Someone tries too hard rigging an election so royalty can be brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: To overexert is to strain oneself by expending more effort than is wise.

clue.text: This moves around, but to no effect?

definitions.text: This moves around, but to no effect?

blocks.note: surface reading: a part or muscle that turns about an axis
setter's reading: turning the word around changes nothing, since it reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: Something spins about uselessly, going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, so moving it around (reading it backwards) has no effect on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is any device or muscle that turns something round about an axis.

clue.text: 1000 are encircling a Spanish city

indicators.note: encircling means surrounding, so the earlier letters go around the single letter that follows

blocks.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
A is the symbol for the are, a metric unit of area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thousand of something gather round a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAND plus A for 'are' makes GRANDA, which encircles the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia, southern Spain, home of the Alhambra.

clue.text: Realist returned mid-morning?

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: ten a.m. is the middle of the morning

explanation.surface: A pragmatic person came back at around ten in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a French painter associated with the Realist movement before Impressionism.

clue.text: Extremely thin pointer found in home

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: an arrow points the way
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A very slender indicator is discovered in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowest is the superlative of narrow, meaning thinnest of all.

clue.text: Mobile in a jacket pocket finally stolen

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of that word is wanted
something stolen is taken away, so that letter is removed from the garment

blocks.note: taken as written
a gilet is a sleeveless jacket
the last letter of pocket

explanation.surface: A mobile phone was in a jacket pocket, and in the end it got nicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' looks like a phone but is the adjective meaning nimble.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile and mobile both describe someone able to move quickly and easily.

clue.text: Coaches someone who puts effort in to cycle

indicators.note: to cycle is to go round, so the first letter is carried round to the end of the word

blocks.note: someone who strains is putting in effort

explanation.surface: Fitness coaches are people who work hard on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the S of STRAINER from front to back gives the answer; the surface makes 'cycle' sound like riding a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainers are coaches who instruct athletes or teams.

clue.text: Plant with unusual base fashionable, we hear

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary order, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged
what we hear is only the spoken form, so the word is spelt differently from how it sounds

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
e is the base of natural logarithms
current means in fashion now

explanation.surface: A plant with an odd-looking foot is said to be trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' is the mathematical base e, not the bottom of the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The white currant is a shrub, a pale-fruited variety of redcurrant.

clue.text: New slope developing

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
an ascent is an upward slope

explanation.surface: A newly built incline is being developed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence and beginning to grow.

clue.text: China to free old city

indicators.note: free here is a verb meaning to release, so the letters are let loose to form a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A call for China to liberate an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was an ancient Hellenistic city, now Antakya in Turkey.

clue.text: Boss almost making mistake

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short of its end

blocks.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: The manager very nearly commits a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is an embarrassing social blunder.

clue.text: Superficial fool with virus flounders

indicators.note: to flounder is to thrash about clumsily, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shallow idiot who has caught a bug struggles.
explanation.definitionFit: Frivolous means lacking seriousness or depth, the same as superficial.

clue.text: American highwayman saw Norway in decay

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the proverb and country go within the word for decay

blocks.note: a saw is an old saying
N is Norway's international vehicle code
rot is decay

explanation.surface: A Wild West bandit witnessed Norway falling into ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but it is the noun for a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Road agent was the nineteenth-century American term for a robber who held up stagecoaches.

clue.text: R Smythe's creation, English Everyman, returns unaccompanied

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the word for everyman is read backwards

blocks.note: Reg Smythe drew the British comic strip Andy Capp; matching his initial R, the character becomes A Capp
E is the abbreviation for English
everyman is all people

explanation.surface: A cartoonist's character, an English everyman, comes back by himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Capp is a long-running British newspaper strip about a work-shy northern working man, the everyman of the surface; Everyman is also another crossword series.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappella singing is performed with voices alone, without instrumental accompaniment.

clue.text: Nobleman let off polymath

indicators.note: off means gone bad or not right, so the letters of the short word are jumbled

blocks.note: aristo is short for aristocrat
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A lord released a learned genius.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle wrote on physics, ethics, biology, logic and much else, a classic example of a polymath.

clue.text: Someone who gossips in fashion magazine? About time!

indicators.note: about means around, so the magazine title wraps around the single letter

blocks.note: Tatler is a British society and fashion magazine
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A gossip columnist at a glossy magazine is told it is about time.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatler is a long-established British upmarket magazine about high society and fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattler is a person who tells tales and spreads gossip.

clue.text: Setter backing Iron Lady in charge?

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for the setter is written from right to left

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: The compiler supports the Iron Lady, Margaret Thatcher, as leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' reads as Thatcher's nickname, but the two words split: Iron is wordplay and Lady starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female ruler of an empire, a woman in charge.

clue.text: Father abandons desperate caper

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so those letters are dropped from the next word

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
frantic means desperate

explanation.surface: A dad walks out on a wild escapade.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful or absurd prank, much like a caper.

clue.text: Ultimately, love rat possibly caustic

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: the last letter of love
a rat is one example of a rodent, hence possibly

explanation.surface: In the end, a cheating lover is perhaps acid-tongued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love rat' reads as one tabloid phrase for an unfaithful partner, but love is split off for its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Erodent is an adjective for a substance that eats away or corrodes, as a caustic one does.

clue.text: Evolve contract to dispel resistance

indicators.note: to dispel is to drive away, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: to contract is to reduce in size
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Instructions to grow and shrink so as to overcome opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw out or develop something latent, to bring it to evolve.

clue.text: Briefly visit for Yorkshire pudding?

blocks.note: first meaning: to call in on someone for a short time
second meaning: a light hollow baked batter roll, the American cousin of the British dish

explanation.walkthrough: A Yorkshire pudding is a British batter pudding baked in a hot oven; the question mark admits the American popover is only a close relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop over is the phrasal verb for a quick call, and a popover is a puffed batter bake like a Yorkshire pudding.

clue.text: Careful diner in railway carriage eating for one

indicators.note: something eating takes food inside itself, so the vehicle surrounds the short abbreviation

blocks.note: a van is a railway carriage for luggage or goods
e.g. means for example, for one

explanation.surface: A fussy eater sits in a dining car, eating alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan chooses food carefully, avoiding all animal products.

clue.text: Hand guard sharp spike to stop Lord Sebastian?

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the spike is inserted into the name

blocks.note: a quill is a sharp spine, as on a porcupine
Sebastian Coe, British Olympic champion runner, is a life peer, Lord Coe

explanation.surface: A bodyguard uses a sharp spike to halt a nobleman named Sebastian.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquille is the shell-shaped guard on a fencing sword that protects the hand.

clue.text: Christ's words tally with independent advice, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of advice is used

blocks.note: a log is a running record or tally
I is the abbreviation for independent
the first letter of advice

explanation.surface: Jesus's sayings match up with unbiased guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: Logia are collections of sayings attributed to Jesus, from Greek for words or oracles.

clue.text: Tasmanian dares to shuffle very close

indicators.note: to shuffle cards is to mix their order, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An Australian from Tasmania challenges others to a game of cards at close quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: As near as damnit is an informal British idiom meaning almost exactly, so very close.
